body:
Maria (Support): FYI customer on dedicated pool 'eu2-prod-dedicated-4' reporting intermittent 429 + high tail latency since 03:00 UTC. saw token throttles and stream stalls.

Jin (SRE): thanks, can you paste request IDs + sample logs? also what model / MIG partition used?

Maria (Support): sample request id: req_20260303_0012, model: redwood-7b-v2-q4_1, pool: eu2-prod-dedicated-4, MIG profile: 1g.10gb + 1g.10gb (two partitions on same physical host). stack says 'runtime_throttle: kv_cache_lock' and worker reports 429s.

Arjun (Runtime Eng): kv_cache_lock is unusual, could be KV cache eviction / contention. Any node-level metrics? nvidia-smi output from host?

Maria (Support): attaching snippet:
```
GPU 0: 15%  4096MiB/24576MiB
GPU 1: 97% 22400MiB/24576MiB (MIG slice 1g.10gb high)
Processes: 1 python (pid 3124) heavy
```

Jin (SRE): looks like one MIG slice saturating SM utilization while sibling idle => noisy neighbor. Also saw PCIe Rx throughput spikes in metrics (packets per sec). I'm going to bump autoscaler to add a slot and cordon offending host.

autoscaler-bot: autoscaler: scaling +1 slot in eu2-dedicated pool (reason: sustained tail latency > SLO). action_id: act_1833456123_1

Arjun (Runtime Eng): please collect 'perf' traces and runtime logs for that host (path /var/log/redwood/runtime/*.log). Also capture kernel scheduler trace (ftrace) if possible. Suspect kernel-level preemption and L3 cache thrash.

Maria (Support): repro steps from customer: high concurrency with streaming, 40 req/s each with long context (~1024 tokens). curl snippet:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \
 -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-v2-q4_1","prompt":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":1024,"stream":true}'
```

Arjun (Runtime Eng): that's heavy small-batch streaming, continuous KV growth. For MIG sibling fairness we have heuristics but this shows SM saturation plus memory bandwidth hog. Quick mitigation: pin requests to different model variant or enforce per-GPU QoS via cgroup CPU/GPU throttle.

Priya (CS): Customer is on committed reserved plan, they flagged production impact. They want a timeline and root cause.

Jin (SRE): short-term: cordon host, reschedule affected slots to other hosts; long-term: add sibling-aware placement (avoid mixing heavy streaming and large batch workloads on same host), and tune autoscaler policy to trigger earlier based on SM% and PCIe metrics.

Arjun (Runtime Eng): I'll open a runtime issue with repro: include trace, nvidia-smi, telemetry. assign to eng-runtime. Issue: RUNTIME-1429.

Maria (Support): Logged RUNTIME-1429 with initial artifacts + customer repro. Customer updated: they saw 429 spikes at 03:12-03:18 UTC and requests resumed after we scaled.

Jin (SRE): closing loop: cordoned host id host-eu2-112, moved slots, verifying tail now back to normal. last 10m p95 token latency down from 1.8s to 0.35s.

Arjun (Runtime Eng): plan: deliver sibling-aware placement + KV backpressure in next sprint, ETA 3 weeks. Also propose rate-limit guard for streaming endpoints to protect MIG neighbors.

Maria (Support): thanks team. PR for docs update and mitigation notes? I'll reply to customer.

logs-bot: archived logs for req_20260303_0012 -> s3://redwood-logs/2026/03/03/req_20260303_0012.log

Maria (Support): Customer follow-up: appreciate quick action, requested SLA incident report. I'll coordinate with Jin for postmortem.

Jin (SRE): will draft postmortem (short) and notify affected customers. assigning to postmortems channel after final artifacts.

Arjun (Runtime Eng): adding perf counters to telemetry to detect this pattern automatically.

Maria (Support): closing ticket with customer pending postmortem. :white_check_mark:
